B03C001.summary: The Pandavas leave Hastinapura after losing at dice, with Draupadi and their attendants, heading north. Citizens angry at Duryodhana and his allies follow them out and beg to go along. Yudhishthira asks them to return and care for the elders left behind, and the people reluctantly turn back. The chapter opens the forest exile by showing the brothers' departure and their first night on the Ganges bank.

scenes.B03C001S01: Janamejaya asks how the Pandavas and Draupadi fared in exile, and Vaisampayana describes their departure from Hastinapura and the citizens' anger at Duryodhana.
scenes.B03C001S02: The citizens follow the Pandavas and plead to go with them, Yudhishthira sends them back, and the Pandavas spend their first night by the Ganges.

shots.B03C001S01H01: Section heading: the Aranyaka Parva, the Book of the Forest.
shots.B03C001S01H02: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Saraswati, and the word Jaya is to be spoken.
shots.B03C001S01H03: Janamejaya asks how his ancestors, the sons of Pritha, lived in the forest after their defeat at dice, and how Draupadi bore her exile.
shots.B03C001S01H04: Vaisampayana says the Pandavas left Hastinapura by the northern gate with Draupadi, their attendants and servants.
shots.B03C001S01H05: The citizens lament that Duryodhana and his allies will ruin the kingdom, and they resolve to follow the Pandavas.
shots.B03C001S02H01: The citizens go after the Pandavas and address them with joined hands.
shots.B03C001S02H02: The citizens plead to go with the Pandavas, arguing that good company brings virtue and that they do not want to live under the Kuru king.
shots.B03C001S02H03: Yudhishthira thanks them but asks them to go back and look after Bhishma, Dhritarashtra, Vidura, his mother and the others left in the city.
shots.B03C001S02H04: The people wail and, though unwillingly, turn back and take leave of the Pandavas.
shots.B03C001S02H05: The Pandavas reach the great banyan tree called Pramana on the Ganges, bathe, and spend the night fasting on water, with Brahmanas keeping them company.

B03C002.summary: On the morning the Pandavas enter the forest, Yudhishthira warns the Brahmana companions of its dangers and offers them release, but they refuse. Yudhishthira feels shame at having others suffer for his sake. The sage Saunaka consoles him with a long teaching that attachment, desire and wealth cause suffering and that contentment and detachment bring peace. Yudhishthira answers that he wants wealth only to support Brahmanas and guests, and Saunaka closes with advice on duty and austerity.

scenes.B03C002S01: Yudhishthira warns the Brahmanas about the forest and asks them to turn back, they refuse, and he admits his shame at his brothers' hardship.
scenes.B03C002S02: Saunaka teaches Yudhishthira about detachment and the dangers of desire and wealth, Yudhishthira explains his view of duty to guests, and Saunaka describes the path of the wise.

shots.B03C002S01H01: At dawn the Brahmanas who live on alms stand before the Pandavas, who are about to enter the forest. Yudhishthira warns them of the hardships and tells them to go home.
shots.B03C002S01H02: The Brahmanas refuse to leave, saying the gods favor those who serve them and that the Pandavas' path is theirs too.
shots.B03C002S01H03: Yudhishthira says he honors Brahmanas, but he is ashamed to ask his grieving brothers to do the hard work of gathering food.
shots.B03C002S01H04: The Brahmanas promise to find their own food and to comfort the king with prayers and pleasant talk.
shots.B03C002S01H05: Yudhishthira accepts, but says it shames him that good men must toil for food because of him, and he curses the sons of Dhritarashtra.
shots.B03C002S02H01: Saunaka, a learned Brahmana, tells the weeping king that the wise are not undone by loss. He recites Janaka's teaching that attachment causes suffering, wealth brings fear and desire never ends, and contentment is the highest good.
shots.B03C002S02H02: Yudhishthira replies that he wants wealth only to support Brahmanas and guests, not out of greed, and he describes a householder's duty to share food and to honor guests.
shots.B03C002S02H03: Saunaka says the world is full of contradictions, and describes how the senses lead people through desire and resolve into ignorance and endless rebirth.
shots.B03C002S02H04: Saunaka sets out the path of the wise: act without attachment, follow the eight duties, practise yoga and austerity, and serve the Brahmanas. The section ends with this counsel.

B03C003.summary: Yudhishthira asks his priest Dhaumya what to do about the Brahmanas who follow him into exile and whom he cannot feed. Dhaumya teaches that the sun sustains all creatures and urges him to worship Surya. Yudhishthira sings a hymn of praise in the Ganges, and the sun grants him an inexhaustible food supply and promises his kingdom back after fourteen years. The Pandavas then feed the Brahmanas and set out for the Kamyaka woods.

scenes.B03C003S01: Yudhishthira asks Dhaumya how to feed the Brahmanas, Dhaumya explains the sun's role and gives a hymn of its names, and Yudhishthira prepares to worship in the river.
scenes.B03C003S02: The sun appears, grants Yudhishthira a copper vessel and a promise of food and a return to the kingdom, and the Pandavas feed the Brahmanas before setting out for Kamyaka.

shots.B03C003S01H01: Yudhishthira tells Dhaumya that the Brahmanas following him into the forest are more than he can support, and asks what he should do.
shots.B03C003S01H02: Dhaumya explains that the sun feeds all creatures through rain and crops, and urges Yudhishthira to take refuge in him and practise austerity, as past kings did.
shots.B03C003S01H03: Janamejaya asks how Yudhishthira worshipped the sun for the sake of the Brahmanas.
shots.B03C003S01H04: Vaisampayana introduces a hymn of the sun's 108 names, which Dhaumya recites, and says it brings prosperity, children, learning and freedom from grief.
shots.B03C003S01H05: Yudhishthira bathes, stands in the Ganges facing the sun, and begins his hymn of praise.
shots.B03C003S02H01: Yudhishthira's hymn calls the sun the eye and soul of the universe and lists the gods and beings who honour him, and his power over seasons and the cosmic cycles.
shots.B03C003S02H02: The sun appears and promises Yudhishthira food for years, gives him a copper vessel that keeps the food inexhaustible, and says he will regain his kingdom in the fourteenth year.
shots.B03C003S02H03: Vaisampayana says the hymn grants a devotee what he asks, and traces its passage from Brahma to Indra, then Narada, then Dhaumya, and finally Yudhishthira.
shots.B03C003S02H04: Yudhishthira bathes, embraces his brothers, and cooks with Draupadi. The food multiplies, the Brahmanas and brothers are fed, and the food runs out only after Draupadi eats.
shots.B03C003S02H05: After feeding the Brahmanas and performing sacrifices with Dhaumya, the Pandavas set out with the Brahmanas for the Kamyaka woods.

B03C004.summary: After the Pandavas leave, Dhritarashtra asks Vidura how to keep the citizens on his side. Vidura urges him to restore the Pandavas' share of the kingdom and to set aside Duryodhana, warning that the Kurus will be destroyed otherwise. Dhritarashtra refuses, saying he cannot abandon his own son, and sends Vidura away. Vidura goes to the Pandavas, convinced that the race is doomed.

scenes.B03C004S01: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura for counsel, Vidura urges justice to the Pandavas, Dhritarashtra refuses and dismisses him, and Vidura leaves for the Pandavas.

shots.B03C004S01H01: Dhritarashtra, sorrowful after the Pandavas leave, asks Vidura what the Kauravas should do to keep the citizens from turning against them.
shots.B03C004S01H02: Vidura advises him to act with justice, to restore what was taken from the Pandavas, and to set Duryodhana aside, warning that Bhima and Arjuna will destroy the Kurus otherwise.
shots.B03C004S01H03: Dhritarashtra rejects this counsel, saying Duryodhana is his own flesh and blood and he cannot abandon him, and tells Vidura to go wherever he likes.
shots.B03C004S01H04: Dhritarashtra goes into the inner apartments, and Vidura, saying the race is doomed, goes off to the Pandavas.

B03C005.summary: The Pandavas move through holy places to the Kamyaka forest on the Saraswati, where Munis visit them. Vidura arrives alone, and Yudhishthira, fearing a new dice challenge, asks what he has come for. Vidura reports that Dhritarashtra has rejected his advice and repeats counsel to build allies, share wealth with them and speak truthfully. Yudhishthira agrees to follow it.

scenes.B03C005S01: The Pandavas settle in Kamyaka forest, Vidura visits and reports Dhritarashtra's rejection, and he repeats advice about patience and allies, which Yudhishthira accepts.

shots.B03C005S01H01: The Pandavas travel from the Ganges through holy places to Kamyaka forest, where Munis visit them. Vidura arrives in a single chariot, and Yudhishthira, fearing Sakuni has sent him to propose another dice game, wonders what he wants.
shots.B03C005S01H02: Yudhishthira welcomes Vidura, who sits among them and begins to explain Dhritarashtra's conduct.
shots.B03C005S01H03: Vidura reports that Dhritarashtra rejected his advice and repeats it: wait patiently, gather adherents, share your wealth with them, and speak truthfully.
shots.B03C005S01H04: Yudhishthira says he will follow Vidura's counsel and the guidance he gives about time and place.

B03C006.summary: Dhritarashtra regrets his harshness to Vidura and sends Sanjaya to the Pandavas to bring him back. Sanjaya finds Vidura with Yudhishthira at Kamyaka, and Yudhishthira lets him return. Dhritarashtra welcomes Vidura with affection and apology, and Vidura forgives him, and the two brothers are glad to be reconciled.

scenes.B03C006S01: Dhritarashtra regrets his anger at Vidura and sends Sanjaya to fetch him. Vidura returns to Hastinapura, and the two brothers apologise and are reconciled.

shots.B03C006S01H01: Dhritarashtra regrets driving Vidura away, collapses senseless at the door of the hall, and orders Sanjaya to bring Vidura back, saying he will die if Sanjaya fails.
shots.B03C006S01H02: Sanjaya reaches Kamyaka and finds Yudhishthira with Vidura among Brahmanas and brothers. He passes on the king's request, and Yudhishthira agrees to let Vidura go.
shots.B03C006S01H03: Vidura returns to Hastinapura. Dhritarashtra embraces him and asks forgiveness for his harsh words, and Vidura forgives him, explaining that he favours the Pandavas because they are in distress.
shots.B03C006S01H04: The two brothers apologise to one another and are greatly happy.

B03C007.summary: Duryodhana, angry that Vidura has returned and calmed the king, gathers Sakuni, Karna and Dussasana and vows to undo the Pandavas' return. Sakuni advises patience and watching, while Karna urges an armed attack on the exiles in the forest. The princes set out, but Vyasa, seeing their plan by his insight, stops them and goes to Dhritarashtra.

scenes.B03C007S01: Duryodhana, enraged by Vidura's return, consults Sakuni, Karna and Dussasana, Karna urges an armed raid, and the princes set out until Vyasa turns them back.

shots.B03C007S01H01: Duryodhana, distressed that Vidura has come back, calls on Sakuni, Karna and Dussasana and vows he will die rather than see the Pandavas prosper again.
shots.B03C007S01H02: Sakuni says the Pandavas will keep their pledge and will not accept recall, and advises the Kauravas to act quietly and watch them.
shots.B03C007S01H03: Dussasana agrees with Sakuni. Karna says the Pandavas will not return before their term ends, and if they do, the Kauravas should defeat them at dice again.
shots.B03C007S01H04: Duryodhana turns away, gloomy. Karna, angry, urges the princes to attack the Pandavas in the forest while they are in distress.
shots.B03C007S01H05: The princes applaud, arm themselves and set out, but Vyasa stops them and then goes to the king.

B03C008.summary: Vyasa comes to Dhritarashtra and warns that once the Pandavas' exile ends they will remember their wrongs and strike back. He urges the king to restrain Duryodhana while there is still time. The chapter is a short, direct warning from the sage.

scenes.B03C008S01: Vyasa warns Dhritarashtra that the Pandavas will seek revenge after their exile and urges him to restrain Duryodhana before it is too late.

shots.B03C008S01H01: Vyasa warns Dhritarashtra that the dishonest dice defeat of the Pandavas will bring revenge after thirteen years, and urges him to restrain Duryodhana, since the Kauravas will suffer if he does not. He asks what Bhishma, Drona and Vidura think.

B03C009.summary: Dhritarashtra admits he cannot cast off his son Duryodhana even though he disliked the dice game. Vyasa tells the tale of Indra and Suravi, in which the mother cow weeps over her weakest calf, to show that a parent's love falls most on the weak. He applies the lesson to the Kurus and urges Duryodhana to make peace with the Pandavas.

scenes.B03C009S01: Dhritarashtra confesses his parental weakness, Vyasa tells the story of Indra and Suravi, and then urges peace with the Pandavas.

shots.B03C009S01H01: Dhritarashtra says he disliked the dice game but was pushed into it by fate, and admits that out of paternal love he cannot cast off his foolish son Duryodhana.
shots.B03C009S01H02: Vyasa agrees that a son is precious and begins a story: the mother cow Suravi weeps in heaven as a farmer beats one of her calves while it pulls the plough.
shots.B03C009S01H03: Indra asks why she grieves for one calf when thousands of her offspring suffer. She replies that she loves all equally but pities the weakest most.
shots.B03C009S01H04: Indra is moved and sends rain to stop the farmer's work. Vyasa applies the lesson to Dhritarashtra and urges him to favour the weaker Pandavas and to have Duryodhana make peace with them.

B03C010.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Vyasa's help, and the sage Maitreya arrives, having seen Yudhishthira at Kamyaka. Maitreya urges Duryodhana to make peace, citing Bhima's feats against Rakshasas and Jarasandha. Duryodhana sneers in silence, so Maitreya curses him that Bhima will break his thigh in the coming war. Maitreya then refuses to say more, sending Dhritarashtra to Vidura for the story of Kirmira.

scenes.B03C010S01: Vyasa sends Maitreya to counsel the Kauravas, who arrives and urges peace, recounting Bhima's exploits.
scenes.B03C010S02: Duryodhana mocks the sage, who curses him, Dhritarashtra asks about Kirmira, and Maitreya leaves.

shots.B03C010S01H01: Dhritarashtra tells the sage that Vidura, Bhishma and Drona have already counselled him, and asks for help in restraining Duryodhana.
shots.B03C010S01H02: Vyasa says Maitreya is coming to advise Duryodhana, and warns that if his counsel is ignored the sage will curse the prince.
shots.B03C010S01H03: Maitreya arrives and is welcomed with honour. Dhritarashtra asks about the Pandavas and whether the Kurus will keep their brotherly bonds.
shots.B03C010S01H04: Maitreya says he met Yudhishthira at Kamyaka, heard of the disaster caused by the dice game, and came out of affection to warn that the quarrel must stop.
shots.B03C010S01H05: Maitreya urges Duryodhana to make peace, recalling how Bhima killed the Rakshasas Hidimba and Kirmira and the warrior Jarasandha.
shots.B03C010S02H01: Duryodhana stays silent and scornful, scratching the ground and slapping his thigh. Maitreya, angered, curses him that Bhima will break his thigh in the war.
shots.B03C010S02H02: Dhritarashtra tries to calm the sage. Maitreya says the curse will stand unless Duryodhana makes peace with the Pandavas.
shots.B03C010S02H03: Dhritarashtra asks how Bhima slew Kirmira.
shots.B03C010S02H04: Maitreya refuses to speak further, says Vidura will tell the story, and leaves. Duryodhana goes out, troubled by the news of Kirmira's death.

B03C011.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura how Bhima killed the Rakshasa Kirmira. Vidura describes how Kirmira, brother of Vaka, blocked the Pandavas at midnight in Kamyaka forest with illusions and vowed to devour Bhima. Bhima fought him with a tree and then wrestled him to death, and the Pandavas moved on to the Dwaita woods. Dhritarashtra sighs and falls into thought at the tale.

scenes.B03C011S01: Dhritarashtra asks about Kirmira, Vidura describes the Rakshasa's ambush and his challenge to the Pandavas.
scenes.B03C011S02: Bhima fights and kills Kirmira, the Pandavas move on, and Dhritarashtra sighs at the news.

shots.B03C011S01H01: Section heading: the Kirmirabadha Parva, the Book of the Slaying of Kirmira.
shots.B03C011S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura to describe how Kirmira and Bhima met in combat.
shots.B03C011S01H03: Vidura says the Pandavas, after their defeat at dice, reached Kamyaka after dark, where a Rakshasa blocked their path with illusions that Dhaumya dispelled with mantras.
shots.B03C011S01H04: The Rakshasa demands to know who they are. Yudhishthira names himself, and the Rakshasa, Vaka's brother, boasts that he will eat them.
shots.B03C011S01H05: Kirmira says he has long sought to avenge Vaka and Hidimba on Bhima, and vows to devour Bhima before Yudhishthira's eyes.
shots.B03C011S02H01: Yudhishthira rebukes the Rakshasa. Bhima fights him with a tree, then wrestles him down, binds and crushes him, and kills him, after which the Pandavas leave for the Dwaita woods.
shots.B03C011S02H02: Vidura says the Pandavas settled peacefully in the cleared forest with Draupadi, and that he himself saw the dead Rakshasa and heard the tale from the Brahmanas.
shots.B03C011S02H03: Dhritarashtra sighs in sorrow and falls into thought at the account of Kirmira's death.

B03C012.summary: Hearing of the Pandavas' exile, Krishna and many allies visit them in the forest, and Krishna vows that the Kauravas will die and Yudhishthira will be restored. Arjuna calms him by recounting Krishna's divine deeds, and Krishna replies that he and Arjuna are one. Draupadi then weeps and recounts the insult in the assembly and the Kauravas' earlier plots, and Dhrishtadyumna and Krishna vow revenge. The chapter turns the exile into a political and personal grievance that the allies take up.

scenes.B03C012S01: Allies arrive in the forest, Krishna vows to destroy the Kauravas, Arjuna calms him by praising his deeds, and Krishna says he and Arjuna are inseparable.
scenes.B03C012S02: Draupadi laments the insult in the assembly and the Kauravas' earlier plots, Krishna and Arjuna promise to restore her, and Dhrishtadyumna vows to kill the Kaurava leaders.
scenes.B03C012S03: The assembled heroes turn to Krishna, who prepares to speak.

shots.B03C012S01H02: Hearing of the exile, the Bhojas, Vrishnis, Andhakas, Panchalas, Dhrishtaketu and the Kaikeyas come to the forest. Krishna vows that Duryodhana, Karna, Dussasana and Sakuni will be slain and Yudhishthira restored.
shots.B03C012S01H03: Krishna's anger grows until Arjuna steps in to calm him by recounting Krishna's deeds.
shots.B03C012S01H04: Arjuna lists Krishna's feats across many ages, including long austerities, sacrifices, the slaying of demons, and his role as creator and sustainer of the world.
shots.B03C012S01H05: Krishna replies that he and Arjuna are the sages Nara and Narayana, born on earth for a purpose, and that no one can tell them apart.
shots.B03C012S02H01: Draupadi appeals to Krishna, recalls her humiliation in the assembly and the Pandavas' failure to defend her, and lists the Kauravas' earlier plots against the brothers.
shots.B03C012S02H02: Draupadi asks why the mighty heroes sit still while weak enemies treat her with contempt, and recalls her own noble birth and marriage.
shots.B03C012S02H03: Draupadi weeps and says she has no husband, son, brother or father to protect her, and asks Krishna for his protection.
shots.B03C012S02H04: Krishna promises Draupadi that he will act for the Pandavas and make her queen again, and Arjuna assures her the same.
shots.B03C012S02H05: Dhrishtadyumna vows that he will kill Drona, Sikhandin will kill Bhishma, Bhima will kill Duryodhana, and Arjuna will kill Karna, with Rama and Krishna as allies.
shots.B03C012S03H01: The assembled heroes turn towards Vasudeva, who begins to speak.

B03C013.summary: Krishna tells Yudhishthira that had he been at Dwaraka, he would have prevented the dice game by warning of its evils and, if need be, by force. He explains that he learned of the disaster from Yuyudhana and came as fast as he could. He grieves that the brothers now suffer and that he has come to see them.

scenes.B03C013S01: Krishna explains that he would have stopped the dice game had he been present and that he has come to the brothers now that he has heard of their plight.

shots.B03C013S01H01: Krishna says that had he been at Dwaraka he would have stopped the dice game, by warning of its evils and by force if necessary. He says he came as soon as he learned of their plight from Yuyudhana, and grieves to see the brothers in distress.

B03C014.summary: Yudhishthira asks Krishna where he was while away from Dwaraka. Krishna explains that Salwa, avenging Sisupala, whom Krishna killed at the Rajasuya sacrifice, raided the empty city and killed many young Vrishnis. Krishna chased him to an island in the ocean, and returned to Hastinapura only after hearing of the dice game. The chapter explains why Krishna was absent when the Pandavas needed him.

scenes.B03C014S01: Yudhishthira asks Krishna where he was, and Krishna explains his absence: Salwa's attack on Dwaraka and his own pursuit of the attacker.

shots.B03C014S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Krishna why he was absent from the Anartta country, where he stayed, and what he did while away.
shots.B03C014S01H02: Krishna explains that he killed Sisupala at the Rajasuya, that Salwa then attacked the empty Dwaraka and killed many young Vrishnis, and that Krishna chased him to an ocean island, fought the Danavas there, and came to the Pandavas on hearing of the dice game.

B03C015.summary: Yudhishthira asks Krishna to tell him fully how Salwa was slain. Krishna begins with Salwa's siege of Dwaraka and describes the city's preparations in detail. The walls, traps, weapons, watchmen and rules against drinking show how the Vrishnis readied for the attack.

scenes.B03C015S01: Yudhishthira asks for the full story, and Vasudeva describes Salwa's siege of Dwaraka and the city's defences.

shots.B03C015S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Vasudeva to describe in full the death of the lord of Saubha, since he is not satisfied with the earlier account.
shots.B03C015S01H02: Vasudeva says Salwa came to avenge Sisupala and besieged the city, and describes the Vrishnis' preparations: fortified walls, weapons, guards, pay for the warriors, bans on drinking, and traps outside the walls.

B03C016.summary: Salwa's army marches on Dwaraka and the young Vrishni princes sally out to meet it. Samva drives off Salwa's commander Kshemavriddhi and kills the demon Vegavat, and Charudeshna kills the demon Vivindhya. Salwa returns to the field in force, and Pradyumna steps forward to rally the Yadavas.

scenes.B03C016S01: Salwa's army marches on Dwaraka, the Vrishni princes fight its champions, and Pradyumna rallies the Yadavas as Salwa advances.

shots.B03C016S01H01: Vasudeva describes Salwa's great army, the princes Samva, Charudeshna and Pradyumna sallying out, Samva's defeat of Kshemavriddhi and Vegavat, Charudeshna's killing of Vivindhya, and Pradyumna's call to the Yadavas as Salwa returns.

B03C017.summary: Pradyumna mounts his golden chariot and rides against Salwa, who comes down from his own chariot to fight him. Salwa is struck to the heart by an arrow and falls senseless. He recovers, however, and badly wounds Pradyumna, leaving him insensible on the field.

scenes.B03C017S01: Pradyumna and Salwa fight, Salwa is felled and revives, and Salwa wounds Pradyumna until he falls senseless.

shots.B03C017S01H01: Pradyumna charges Salwa on his golden chariot, Salwa is felled by an arrow to the heart and recovers, and then wounds Pradyumna until he falls senseless on the battlefield.

B03C018.summary: Pradyumna is carried off the field, senseless, by his charioteer, the son of Daruka. When he wakes, he scolds the charioteer for retreating and orders him to turn back. He insists that a Vrishni warrior never flees, and that the shame of running would be worse than death.

scenes.B03C018S01: The charioteer carries the wounded Pradyumna from the field, and Pradyumna wakes, rebukes him, and orders him back into battle.

shots.B03C018S01H01: The Vrishnis despair when Pradyumna falls and the enemy rejoices. Daruka's son drives him off the field, and when he wakes he asks the charioteer why he is retreating.
shots.B03C018S01H02: Pradyumna orders the charioteer to turn back, insisting that a Vrishni never flees and that he would be shamed before his kinsmen if he ran.

B03C019.summary: The charioteer answers that he retreated only to protect the wounded warrior, and he now drives back into the enemy host with great skill. Pradyumna again wounds Salwa, who falls senseless. The gods send Narada and the wind god to stop Pradyumna from killing Salwa, since Salwa is fated to die at Krishna's hand, and Salwa flees across the sky.

scenes.B03C019S01: The charioteer explains his retreat and drives back into battle, Salwa is wounded and falls, and the gods stop Pradyumna from slaying him.

shots.B03C019S01H01: The charioteer explains that he retreated to protect the wounded warrior, and offers to show his skill by driving back into the enemy array.
shots.B03C019S01H02: The charioteer drives with great skill and Pradyumna again wounds Salwa, who falls. Narada and the wind god stop Pradyumna from loosing his deadly arrow, because Salwa is fated to die at Krishna's hand, and Salwa flees across the sky.

B03C020.summary: Krishna, here also called Vasudeva, returns to Dwaraka after the Rajasuya and finds the city mourning Salwa's raid. He vows to kill Salwa, sets out with his army, and follows him to the ocean. There a long battle of arrows and illusions begins, which Krishna meets with counter-illusions and a powerful weapon.

scenes.B03C020S01: Krishna learns of Salwa's raid, sets out to kill him, and fights him at sea through a long contest of arrows and illusions.

shots.B03C020S01H01: Krishna returns to a mourning Dwaraka, learns from Kritavarman of Salwa's raid, vows to slay him, and chases him to the ocean, where a long battle of arrows, illusions and counter-illusions follows.

B03C021.summary: Salwa keeps up his attack, and Krishna's charioteer Daruka is badly wounded. A messenger from Ahuka brings the false report that Salwa has killed Krishna's father Vasudeva in Dwaraka. Krishna is stunned, seeing an illusion of his father falling, and swoons before recovering to fight on.

scenes.B03C021S01: Daruka is wounded and Krishna cheers him, a false message reports that Vasudeva has been killed, and Krishna swoons at an illusion before rising to fight again.

shots.B03C021S01H01: Salwa's weapons wound Daruka badly, and the charioteer says he can no longer hold on. Krishna looks him over and cheers him up.
shots.B03C021S01H02: A messenger from Ahuka arrives with the false news that Salwa has killed Vasudeva in Dwaraka and urges Krishna to stop fighting and defend the city. Krishna is grief-stricken, sees an illusion of his father falling, swoons, and then resumes the battle with arrows.

B03C023.summary: The Pandavas set out into the forest after giving gifts to Brahmanas, and the people of Kurujangala come to bid them farewell. They lament the king's exile and blame Duryodhana, Dussasana, Karna and Sakuni. Arjuna asks the Brahmanas to plead the Pandavas' cause with the ascetics, and the people go home with heavy hearts.

scenes.B03C023S01: The Pandavas enter the forest, and the people of Kurujangala lament their exile, blame the Kauravas, and return home at Arjuna's request.

shots.B03C023S01H01: The Pandavas set out into the forest after giving gifts, and the people of Kurujangala lament their exile, blame Duryodhana and his allies, and beg them to return. Arjuna asks the Brahmanas to plead for them with the ascetics, and the people go home sorrowful.

B03C024.summary: Yudhishthira tells his brothers they must spend the next twelve years in the forest and asks them to find a suitable place. Arjuna suggests the lake of Dwaitavana, rich in flowers and birds, and Yudhishthira agrees. The Pandavas and their Brahmana companions enter the forest and sit down at the foot of a great tree, welcomed by ascetics.

scenes.B03C024S01: Yudhishthira asks for a place to spend twelve years, Arjuna proposes Dwaitavana, and the Pandavas arrive in the forest and are welcomed by ascetics.

shots.B03C024S01H01: Yudhishthira tells his brothers they must live twelve years in the forest and asks them to find a fitting place. Arjuna suggests the lake of Dwaitavana, and Yudhishthira agrees.
shots.B03C024S01H02: The Pandavas go to the lake with many Brahmanas and ascetics, entering a forest of flowering trees, birds and elephants. The ascetics welcome Yudhishthira, who sits under a great tree with his brothers around him.
shots.B03C024S01H03: Heading for Section XXV, which begins the next part of the book.

B03C022.summary: Krishna fights through Salwa's illusions, including a shower of rocks that buries him, and breaks free with the thunderbolt. Daruka urges him to finish Salwa, and Krishna hurls the Sudarsana discus, which destroys the city of Saubha and Salwa himself. Krishna then takes leave of the Pandavas and returns to Dwaraka, while the allies and Brahmanas go their separate ways.

scenes.B03C022S01: Krishna destroys Salwa's illusions and city with the discus, then takes his leave of the Pandavas and returns to Dwaraka, while their allies and the Brahmanas go their ways.

shots.B03C022S01H01: Krishna describes fighting illusory Danavas and an illusory car, being buried under a shower of rocks, and breaking free with the thunderbolt. Daruka urges him to kill Salwa, and Krishna hurls the discus, which destroys Saubha and Salwa, and says he could not come to the dice game in time.
shots.B03C022S01H02: Krishna takes leave of the Pandavas, who honour him, and sets out for Dwaraka with Subhadra and Abhimanyu. Dhrishtadyumna, Dhrishtaketu and the Kaikeyas also depart, while the Brahmanas and people stay with Yudhishthira, who orders his chariot readied.

B03C025.summary: The Pandavas settle in the Dwaita woods, where Dhaumya performs sacrifices and Yudhishthira honours the ascetics. The sage Markandeya visits and, seeing their plight, recalls Rama's exile. He urges Yudhishthira that no one should act wrongly out of pride in his own might, and predicts that Yudhishthira will win back his fortune. The sage then departs to the north.

scenes.B03C025S01: The Pandavas settle in the Dwaita woods, the sage Markandeya visits and recalls Rama's exile to urge restraint, and then he departs northward.

shots.B03C025S01H01: The Pandavas settle in the forest, Yudhishthira and Dhaumya serve the sages, and the old sage Markandeya arrives as a guest. When Markandeya smiles at the sight of them, Yudhishthira asks why, and the sage recalls Rama's dutiful exile and argues that no one should act wrongly out of pride, predicting that Yudhishthira will win back his fortune.
shots.B03C025S01H02: Markandeya blesses the company and sets out to the north.

B03C026.summary: The Dwaita woods fill with Brahmanas performing rites, and Vaka of the Dalvya line counsels Yudhishthira that Kshatriya strength needs Brahmanical wisdom. He cites the fall of the demon king Vali, who wronged the Brahmanas, and urges Yudhishthira to keep a learned Brahmana as an adviser. The assembled sages then honour Yudhishthira for his respect towards the Brahmanas.

scenes.B03C026S01: Vaka praises Brahmanical counsel to Yudhishthira, with the story of Vali as a warning, and the assembled sages honour Yudhishthira.

shots.B03C026S01H01: The woods fill with Brahmanas at their rites, and the Vedic chanting mixes with the twang of the Pandavas' bows. Vaka of the Dalvya line tells Yudhishthira that Kshatriya might needs Brahmanical wisdom, cites Vali's fall after he wronged the Brahmanas, and urges him to keep a learned Brahmana as counsellor.
shots.B03C026S01H02: Many named sages, including Dwaipayana and Narada, praise Yudhishthira and honour him, as Rishis honour Indra in heaven.

B03C027.summary: Draupadi sits with the Pandavas in the forest and grieves for their lost splendour, contrasting their former luxuries with their present hardship. She notes that only four men, Duryodhana, Karna, Sakuni and Dussasana, did not weep at their exile. She asks why Yudhishthira's anger does not blaze up against the Kauravas, and urges him to act, since a Kshatriya who fails to strike back is despised.

scenes.B03C027S01: Draupadi laments the Pandavas' fall, asks why Yudhishthira does not show anger, and urges him to take action against his enemies.

shots.B03C027S01H01: Draupadi laments the Pandavas' fall from luxury, accuses Duryodhana and his allies of cruelty, and asks why Yudhishthira shows no anger at his brothers' hardship. She urges him to act, saying a Kshatriya who does not strike back at the right time is disregarded by all.

B03C028.summary: Draupadi argues that Yudhishthira should now use his might, citing the old tale of Prahlada's counsel to his grandson Vali. Prahlada teaches that neither constant forgiveness nor constant anger is right, and that the wise must act according to time and place. Draupadi concludes that forgiveness is wasted on the Kauravas and that the time has come for action.

scenes.B03C028S01: Draupadi recounts Prahlada's teaching on forgiveness and might, and then argues that now is the time for Yudhishthira to act.

shots.B03C028S01H01: Draupadi tells of Prahlada's advice to Vali: a man who always forgives is despised, robbed by servants and disrespected by all.
shots.B03C028S01H02: Prahlada warns that the constantly angry man loses friends, wealth and respect, so one should use might and forgiveness each at the proper time.
shots.B03C028S01H03: Prahlada lists the occasions for forgiveness, such as a past service, an offence from ignorance, or an offence done by accident, and says might should be used against others.
shots.B03C028S01H04: Draupadi concludes that the time has come for Yudhishthira to show his might against the covetous Kauravas, since forgiveness is not right towards them.

B03C029.summary: Yudhishthira replies at length that anger destroys people, and that a wise man, strong or weak, should conquer wrath and forgive. He cites Kasyapa's praise of forgiveness and argues that the elders will press for peace, so the kingdom may be returned. He concludes that Duryodhana does not deserve the kingdom and that he himself will hold to forgiveness.

scenes.B03C029S01: Yudhishthira argues against anger, quotes Kasyapa on forgiveness, expects peace from the elders, and resolves to forgive.

shots.B03C029S01H01: Yudhishthira argues at length that anger ruins those who feel it and that the wise forgive even when strong, citing Kasyapa's verses in praise of forgiveness. He expects the elders to urge peace and the king to return the kingdom, judges Duryodhana unworthy, and resolves to keep to forgiveness.

B03C030.summary: Draupadi challenges Yudhishthira, arguing that virtue has not protected him despite his generosity and great sacrifices, and that he gambled everything away in an evil hour. She argues that God directs all creatures like puppets and then asks how a just God lets the wicked prosper. She ends by asking whether human might, rather than God, is the true cause of action.

scenes.B03C030S01: Draupadi reproaches Yudhishthira that virtue has failed him, recounts his good deeds, argues that God governs all things, and questions divine justice.

shots.B03C030S01H01: Draupadi laments that virtue has not protected Yudhishthira, though he honoured Brahmanas, performed great sacrifices, and was undone by the dice game. She argues that God moves all creatures like puppets, and asks how God can let the sinful prosper while the good suffer. If God is responsible for every act, she asks, then human might must be the true cause, and she concludes that she grieves for those without might.

B03C031.summary: Yudhishthira answers Draupadi that he acts out of duty and not for the fruit of his acts, and that doubting virtue is a grave fault. He cites the sages, including Markandeya, who gained lasting merit through virtue, and says that a doubter loses both this world and the next. He urges her to put aside doubt, have faith in God, and honour the Vedas.

scenes.B03C031S01: Yudhishthira rejects Draupadi's doubts, argues that virtue is done for its own sake, and urges her to have faith in God and the scriptures.

shots.B03C031S01H01: Yudhishthira says Draupadi speaks like an atheist. He argues that he acts out of duty and not for reward, that doubting virtue leads to a worse rebirth, and that sages such as Markandeya, Vyasa and Narada prove the rewards of virtue. He urges her to put aside doubt, have faith, and honour God.

B03C032.summary: Draupadi replies that she has never scorned religion or God, and that her words are the lament of a grieving woman. She argues that every living creature must act, that fate and chance alone bring only ruin, and that human effort, guided by intelligence and by the fruits of past deeds, is the cause of success. She ends by saying that a person must act with confidence and not despair when results are slow, and recalls the teaching she received as a child.

scenes.B03C032S01: Draupadi defends her views, argues that human action is essential and that success depends on effort, intelligence and circumstance, and recalls her early teaching.

shots.B03C032S01H01: Draupadi says she has never scorned religion or God, and that her grief has made her speak wildly. She argues that every creature must act, that those who rely only on fate or chance are foolish, and that success depends on human effort, intelligence and the fruits of past deeds. She urges action with confidence, and recalls the lessons she heard as a child from her father's Brahmana teacher.

B03C033.summary: Bhima, angry at the forest life, urges Yudhishthira to give up his pledge and take back the kingdom by force. He says the kingdom was won by Duryodhana's unfair dice and that the Pandavas' patience has only made them look weak. He argues at length that virtue, wealth and pleasure must be pursued together, and that a Kshatriya's duty is to fight with might and stratagem.

scenes.B03C033S01: Bhima urges Yudhishthira to abandon the forest life, use might and stratagem to regain the kingdom, and balance virtue, wealth and pleasure.

shots.B03C033S01H01: Bhima, sighing in anger, tells Yudhishthira that the forest life is weak and shameful, that the kingdom was lost to unfair dice, and that he should stop hiding behind his promise and fight.
shots.B03C033S01H02: Bhima continues that a man must balance virtue, wealth and pleasure, that a Kshatriya's duty is might and stratagem, and that Yudhishthira should march on Hastinapura with his brothers and allies to win back the kingdom.

B03C034.summary: Yudhishthira accepts Bhima's anger but explains that Sakuni's trickery won the dice game and that the agreed terms made them exiles for twelve years and a thirteenth year in disguise. He says that breaking a sworn pledge is worse than death, and that the Pandavas must wait for their chance to avenge the wrong. He also reminds Bhima that he once wanted to burn Yudhishthira's hands during the game and was stopped by Arjuna.

scenes.B03C034S01: Yudhishthira answers Bhima, blames Sakuni's trickery and the agreed terms of exile, and refuses to break his promise.

shots.B03C034S01H01: Yudhishthira says he cannot blame Bhima's harsh words, but explains that Sakuni cheated him at dice and that the agreed terms bound them to twelve years in the forest and a year in disguise. He refuses to break his oath, says Bhima's anger is misplaced, and asks him to wait for a better time and to remember that he once wanted to burn the king's hands and was stopped by Arjuna.

B03C035.summary: Bhima presses Yudhishthira to act at once, arguing that life is short and that waiting thirteen years only brings death closer. He says the Pandavas will be discovered by spies and by the kings they have wronged, and that thirteen months in the forest should be counted as thirteen years. He calls on Yudhishthira to fight, since battle is the Kshatriya's duty.

scenes.B03C035S01: Bhima argues that waiting is pointless, the Pandavas will be found out, and the Kshatriya must fight now.

shots.B03C035S01H01: Bhima argues that life is brief and uncertain, so waiting for thirteen years is pointless, and that the Pandavas will be recognised and betrayed by spies and vanquished kings. He says they have already spent thirteen months in the forest, calls Yudhishthira's forbearance misplaced, and urges him to fight, since that is the Kshatriya's duty.

B03C036.summary: Yudhishthira weighs Bhima's counsel and warns that rash action will fail against the Kaurava champions and their allied kings. Vyasa arrives, promises to dispel Yudhishthira's fear, and teaches him a sacred science, advising Arjuna to seek weapons from the gods. The Pandavas then leave Dwaitavana for Kamyaka and resume their forest life.

scenes.B03C036S01: Yudhishthira answers Bhima's rashness, Vyasa arrives and teaches him a sacred science, and the Pandavas move back to Kamyaka.

shots.B03C036S01H01: Yudhishthira sighs and reflects that true virtue is hard to know, and that he cannot force it aside like crushing a mountain. He settles on a course and answers Bhima without further delay.
shots.B03C036S01H02: Yudhishthira tells Bhima that rash deeds fail, and that the Kaurava champions, including Bhishma, Drona, Karna and the allied kings, are too strong to beat by force alone.
shots.B03C036S01H03: Vyasa arrives, is honoured by the brothers, and says he has come to dispel Yudhishthira's fear of the Kaurava champions by means of a sacred rite.
shots.B03C036S01H04: Vyasa teaches Yudhishthira a science called Pratismriti, tells him Arjuna should seek weapons from Indra and the other gods, and advises the brothers to move to another forest.
shots.B03C036S01H05: Vyasa departs, Yudhishthira keeps the knowledge in his mind, and the Pandavas return to Kamyaka with their Brahmanas to live by archery, hunting and sacred rites.

B03C037.summary: Yudhishthira privately tells Arjuna that Duryodhana's side has the best teachers and weapons, and sends him north to win celestial arms from Indra. He passes on Vyasa's science and sends Arjuna off with blessings from his brothers, Krishna and Draupadi. On the Himalayas, Arjuna is tested by a figure who turns out to be Indra, who urges him to seek the sight of Shiva before he can receive the weapons.

scenes.B03C037S01: Yudhishthira sends Arjuna to Indra for weapons, Arjuna sets out with blessings, and Indra tells him to seek Shiva.

shots.B03C037S01H01: Yudhishthira takes Arjuna aside and explains that the Kaurava side has the best teachers, weapons and allies, and that Arjuna must go north to Indra. He passes on the science Vyasa taught him.
shots.B03C037S01H02: Arjuna sets out fully armed after his brothers and the Brahmanas bless him. Krishna grieves at his departure, recalls Duryodhana's insults, and gives him her blessing.
shots.B03C037S01H03: Draupadi, here also called Krishna, blesses Arjuna as he walks around his brothers and Dhaumya. Arjuna crosses the Himalayas, and at Indrakila an ascetic tells him to lay down his weapons, but he refuses. The ascetic, revealed as Indra, tells him to first behold Shiva before receiving the weapons.

B03C038.summary: Janamejaya asks for the full tale of how Arjuna won weapons and fought Shiva. Arjuna enters the Himalayan forest and practises harsh austerities, eating less and less until he stands on his toes and lives on air alone. Alarmed by the heat of his penance, the sages go to Shiva, who says he knows Arjuna's wish and will grant it.

scenes.B03C038S01: Janamejaya asks for the story of Arjuna's weapons and his meeting with Shiva, and Vaisampayana describes Arjuna's penance and the sages' appeal to Shiva.

shots.B03C038S01H02: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana to tell in full how Arjuna gained weapons, how he entered the solitary forest, and how he fought with the god Bhava.
shots.B03C038S01H03: Vaisampayana agrees to tell of Arjuna's meeting with the three-eyed god and his contact with the god's person.
shots.B03C038S01H04: Arjuna sets out for the Himalayas to see Indra and Shiva, enters the forest with heavenly signs, and practises austerities that grow harsher, from fruit to fortnightly meals to air alone, standing on his toes. Alarmed by the heat of his penance, the sages go to Shiva, who says he knows Arjuna's wish and will grant it.
shots.B03C038S01H05: The truthful sages hear Shiva's words and return to their homes.

B03C039.summary: Shiva comes to the Himalayas disguised as a Kirata hunter, with Uma and a band of attendants, just as a demon in boar form attacks Arjuna. Both Arjuna and the hunter shoot the boar and quarrel over it, and their duel becomes fierce. Arjuna's weapons fail, the hunter's blows leave him senseless, and Arjuna recovers, makes a clay image of the god, and finds his garland on the hunter's head. Shiva then reveals himself, pardons him and promises a weapon.

scenes.B03C039S01: Shiva, disguised as a Kirata, duels Arjuna over a demon boar, Arjuna recognises his garland on the hunter, and Shiva reveals himself and promises a weapon.

shots.B03C039S01H01: Shiva comes down to the Himalayas as a Kirata hunter with Uma and attendants. The demon Muka, in boar form, attacks Arjuna, and both Arjuna and the hunter shoot it, each claiming it. Their duel is fierce: Arjuna's arrows, sword and then his bare fists fail, the hunter's blows leave him senseless, and when he revives he makes a clay image of Bhava and finds his garland on the hunter's crown. Shiva, pleased, says he will grant him an irresistible weapon.
shots.B03C039S01H02: Arjuna kneels before the god, praises him as the cause of all things, and begs pardon for the fight he began in ignorance.
shots.B03C039S01H03: Shiva forgives Arjuna and embraces him, and then speaks again.

B03C040.summary: Shiva tells Arjuna that he was Nara, the friend of Narayana, and returns the Gandiva bow and inexhaustible quivers that he had taken from him by illusion. Arjuna asks for the Brahmasira weapon so he can win the coming war against Karna, Bhishma, Kripa and Drona. Shiva gives him the Pasupata weapon, warns that it must be used only against a worthy foe, and teaches him its mysteries before departing with Uma.

scenes.B03C040S01: Shiva restores Arjuna's bow and quivers, Arjuna asks for a fearsome weapon, and Shiva grants the Pasupata with a warning and departs.

shots.B03C040S01H01: Shiva tells Arjuna that he was once Nara, friend of Narayana, and that he himself had taken the Gandiva from him by illusion. He now restores the bow and the inexhaustible quivers, saying Arjuna's body will be free of pain and that he may ask a boon.
shots.B03C040S01H02: Arjuna asks for the Brahmasira, a weapon that can destroy the universe, so that he can win the coming battle against Karna, Bhishma, Kripa and Drona.
shots.B03C040S01H03: Shiva agrees to give Arjuna the Pasupata weapon, which no god knows, and warns that it must not be used against a weak foe, since it could destroy the world.
shots.B03C040S01H04: Arjuna asks to be taught, and Shiva teaches him the weapon's mysteries. The weapon attends Arjuna, the earth trembles, and Shiva restores Arjuna's body before giving him the Gandiva and departing with Uma.

B03C041.summary: After Shiva vanishes, the guardians of the world, Varuna, Kubera, Yama and Indra, come to the mountain to see Arjuna. Each gives him a celestial weapon, and Indra promises to take him to heaven to receive his full arms. Arjuna worships the gods, who depart, and he feels that his purpose is fulfilled.

scenes.B03C041S01: The guardians of the world gather before Arjuna and each grant him a celestial weapon, and Indra promises to take him to heaven.
scenes.B03C041S02: Arjuna, having obtained the weapons, feels his purpose is fulfilled.

shots.B03C041S01H01: Shiva vanishes and Arjuna rejoices that he has seen and touched the god. Varuna, Kubera, Yama and Indra on his elephant come to the mountain, and Yama, reminding Arjuna that he was once Nara, promises he will defeat Bhishma and Karna and offers him his mace.
shots.B03C041S01H02: Arjuna receives Yama's weapon and its mysteries. Varuna then offers his nooses and the Varuna weapons, recalling how they once bound many Daityas.
shots.B03C041S01H03: Kubera gives Arjuna the celestial weapon Antardhana, which can put a foe to sleep, and says Arjuna is worthy to hold it.
shots.B03C041S01H04: Indra tells Arjuna that he has already reached the stature of a god, but must come to heaven to receive the celestial weapons, and says his chariot with Matali will soon come down for him.
shots.B03C041S01H05: Arjuna worships the assembled guardians, who return the worship and depart to their own realms.
shots.B03C041S02H01: Arjuna, having obtained the weapons, is filled with pleasure and regards himself as having achieved his desire.

B03C042.summary: Indra sends his chariot, driven by Matali, to bring Arjuna up to heaven to receive the celestial weapons. Arjuna insists that Matali mount first, bids farewell to Mount Mandara, and rides up through the realms of the virtuous and the heroic dead. He reaches Amaravati, the city of Indra.

scenes.B03C042S01: Indra's chariot arrives for Arjuna, Matali invites him aboard, Arjuna bids farewell to Mount Mandara, and he rides up through heaven to Amaravati.

shots.B03C042S01H01: Section heading: the Indralokagamana Parva, the Book of Going to Indra's World.
shots.B03C042S01H02: Indra's splendid chariot, driven by Matali, comes down through the clouds, bristling with celestial weapons. Matali tells Arjuna that Indra's father has sent for him so the gods can see him and he can receive weapons.
shots.B03C042S01H03: Arjuna asks Matali to mount first, since the chariot cannot be ridden by anyone without ascetic merit.
shots.B03C042S01H04: Arjuna bathes in the Ganges, performs his rites, and bids farewell to Mount Mandara, then rides up past the lights of the virtuous and the heroic dead, the Gandharvas and the elephant Airavata, until he reaches Amaravati.

B03C043.summary: Arjuna enters Amaravati, a city of flowers and celestial gardens reserved for the virtuous, and is welcomed by the gods, Gandharvas and sages. Indra embraces him and seats him on his own throne, delighting in his son's splendour while heavenly dancers perform.

scenes.B03C043S01: Arjuna enters Indra's city, is greeted by the gods and sages, and is seated beside Indra while Apsaras dance.

shots.B03C043S01H01: Arjuna enters Amaravati, a city of celestial gardens and flowers reserved for the virtuous, and is greeted by the gods, Gandharvas and sages. Indra embraces him, seats him on his own throne, and delights in the sight of his son while heavenly dancers perform.

B03C044.summary: Arjuna stays in Indra's palace for five years, receiving the thunderbolt and other celestial weapons. Indra then sends him to learn celestial music and dance from the Gandharva Chitrasena. Arjuna's mind stays restless, troubled by thoughts of his brothers, his mother and the unfair dice game.

scenes.B03C044S01: Arjuna receives celestial weapons and lives in heaven for five years, then Indra sends him to learn music and dance from Chitrasena.

shots.B03C044S01H01: The gods honour Arjuna, who receives Indra's thunderbolt and the other celestial weapons, and recalls his brothers. At Indra's command he lives in heaven for five years, surrounded by comfort.
shots.B03C044S01H02: Indra tells Arjuna to learn celestial music and dance from Chitrasena, who becomes his friend and teaches him. Arjuna finds no peace, remembering the dice game, Dussasana and his brothers and mother.

B03C045.summary: Indra notices that Arjuna has looked at the Apsara Urvasi, and sends Chitrasena to ask her to attend Arjuna and teach him the arts of female company. Chitrasena praises Arjuna's virtues in the message, and Urvasi replies that she is already drawn to him and will go to him.

scenes.B03C045S01: Indra sends Chitrasena with a request to Urvasi, who agrees to go to Arjuna.

shots.B03C045S01H01: Indra, seeing Arjuna's glances at Urvasi, sends Chitrasena to ask her to wait upon him and teach him the arts of female company. Chitrasena delivers the message, praising Arjuna's many virtues.
shots.B03C045S01H02: Urvasi replies with a smile that she is already moved by love for Arjuna, and agrees to go to him.

B03C046.summary: Urvasi dresses richly and goes to Arjuna's palace at night, desiring him. Arjuna honours her as a superior and refuses her advances, calling her like his mother. Urvasi, enraged, curses him to live among women as a dancer, without manhood, for a year. Indra tells Arjuna the curse will serve him in the thirteenth year of exile, when the brothers must remain unknown, and Arjuna is relieved and sports in heaven.

scenes.B03C046S01: Urvasi visits Arjuna at night, explains Chitrasena's message, and Arjuna refuses her, calling her as his mother.
scenes.B03C046S02: Urvasi curses Arjuna, Chitrasena and Indra respond, and the curse is turned to benefit in the thirteenth year.

shots.B03C046S01H01: Urvasi bathes, adorns herself and goes at night to Arjuna's palace, her mind fixed on him. Arjuna, bashful, shuts his eyes and offers her the respect due to a superior, asking what she commands.
shots.B03C046S01H02: Urvasi explains that Indra held an assembly at which she and others danced, and that Chitrasena came to her with Indra's request. She says she has long cherished her wish for Arjuna.
shots.B03C046S01H03: Arjuna, embarrassed, covers his ears and says she is to him like a wife of a superior, like his mother Kunti or Indra's queen Sachi, and that he gazed at her only in the thought she was the mother of his race.
shots.B03C046S01H04: Urvasi replies that Apsaras are free in their choice, that the sons of Puru freely enjoy their company, and asks him to accept her.
shots.B03C046S01H05: Arjuna repeats that he sees her as his mother, bows at her feet, and asks her to go back and protect him as a son.
shots.B03C046S02H01: Urvasi, enraged and trembling, curses Arjuna to pass a year among women as a dancer, without manhood and scorned as a eunuch, because he rejected her.
shots.B03C046S02H02: Urvasi returns home. Arjuna tells Chitrasena what happened, and Chitrasena reports it to Indra, who says the curse will serve Arjuna well in the thirteenth year of exile, when the brothers must live unknown.
shots.B03C046S02H03: Relieved of worry about the curse, Arjuna sports in heaven with Chitrasena.
shots.B03C046S02H04: Closing lines: listening to this account of Arjuna's pure conduct frees a man from lust, pride and anger, and carries him to heaven.

B03C047.summary: The sage Lomasa visits Indra's heaven and is puzzled to see Arjuna seated beside Indra. Indra explains that Arjuna is his son, that Nara and Narayana have been reborn on earth, and that the demons called Nivatakavachas threaten the gods. He sends Lomasa to Yudhishthira with a message urging him to visit sacred waters and to be guarded against demons on the road.

scenes.B03C047S01: Lomasa sees Arjuna on Indra's seat, Indra explains Arjuna's divine origin and the threat from the Nivatakavachas, and Lomasa is sent to Yudhishthira in the forest.

shots.B03C047S01H01: Lomasa visits Indra's court and sees Arjuna on Indra's seat, wondering what merit won him that place. Indra explains that Arjuna is his son, that Nara and Narayana were reborn on earth to help the gods against the Nivatakavachas, and sends Lomasa to Yudhishthira with a message that he should visit sacred waters and be guarded from Rakshasas.
shots.B03C047S01H02: Heading for Section XLVIII, the next part of the book.
shots.B03C047S01H03: Arjuna asks Lomasa to protect Yudhishthira, to let him visit holy places, and to give gifts to Brahmanas.
shots.B03C047S01H04: Lomasa agrees, sets out for the earth, and reaches Kamyaka, where he finds Yudhishthira surrounded by ascetics and his brothers.

B03C048.summary: Janamejaya asks how Dhritarashtra reacted to news of Arjuna's feats. Dhritarashtra, having heard from Vyasa, tells Sanjaya that his sons cannot stand against Arjuna, and he foresees a terrible war that may end the Kuru line. He fears that Arjuna's anger, with Krishna as his ally, will be impossible to calm.

scenes.B03C048S01: Janamejaya asks about Dhritarashtra's reaction, and Dhritarashtra tells Sanjaya he fears Arjuna's power and foresees ruin for his sons.

shots.B03C048S01H01: Janamejaya asks what Dhritarashtra said when he heard of Arjuna's feats.
shots.B03C048S01H02: Dhritarashtra, having heard of Arjuna's stay in Indra's abode from Vyasa, asks Sanjaya for details. He calls Duryodhana's policy vulgar, names the warriors who might face Arjuna, and says that Arjuna's arrows will consume his sons and that no one can stand before him.

B03C049.summary: Sanjaya replies that Dhritarashtra's words are true, that the Pandavas are full of rage over Draupadi's humiliation, and that Arjuna has won the favour of the gods, even fighting Shiva as a hunter. He repeats Bhima's vow to smash Duryodhana's thighs. Dhritarashtra laments Karna's cruel words and his sons' folly, and admits that Arjuna, with Krishna as his ally, cannot be conquered.

scenes.B03C049S01: Sanjaya describes the Pandavas' rage and Arjuna's divine feats, and Dhritarashtra laments his sons' folly and Karna's cruelty.

shots.B03C049S01H01: Sanjaya agrees with Dhritarashtra, saying the Pandavas are enraged by Draupadi's shaming and that Arjuna has won the favour of the gods, including Shiva, whom he fought as a hunter. He repeats Bhima's vow to smash Duryodhana's thighs when the thirteen years end.
shots.B03C049S01H02: Dhritarashtra laments that Karna's cruel words have stirred the Pandavas further, says his blind and foolish son listens only to counsellors who indulge his vices, and admits that Arjuna, with Krishna as his ally, cannot be overcome by his sons.

B03C050.summary: Janamejaya asks what food the Pandavas lived on in the forest. Vaisampayana says they hunted deer and fed the Brahmanas first, and that Yudhishthira supported thousands of Snataka Brahmanas. Draupadi fed her husbands and the Brahmanas before eating herself, and the brothers spent five years at Kamyaka, anxious for Arjuna's absence yet busy with study and sacrifice.

scenes.B03C050S01: Janamejaya asks how the Pandavas fed themselves, and Vaisampayana describes their hunting, their feeding of the Brahmanas, and their life at Kamyaka.

shots.B03C050S01H01: Janamejaya asks why Dhritarashtra let Duryodhana provoke the Pandavas, and what food the exiles ate, whether from the wild or from cultivation.
shots.B03C050S01H02: Vaisampayana says the Pandavas hunted deer and shared the meat, feeding Brahmanas first. Yudhishthira supported ten thousand Snataka Brahmanas, Draupadi fed the others before herself, and the brothers hunted in all directions for five years at Kamyaka, anxious for Arjuna, yet busy with study and sacrifice.

B03C051.summary: Dhritarashtra, hearing of the Pandavas' hardy life, is filled with fear and lists their strength, predicting that his army will be destroyed. Sanjaya replies that Krishna visited the forest and promised to restore Yudhishthira and slay Duryodhana and his allies when the exile ends. Dhritarashtra recalls Vidura's warning that the dice game would lead to bloodshed among the Kurus, and fears it is coming true.

scenes.B03C051S01: Dhritarashtra fears the Pandavas' might and his own army's ruin, Sanjaya reports Krishna's promise to restore them, and Dhritarashtra recalls Vidura's warning.

shots.B03C051S01H01: Dhritarashtra, unable to rest, describes the Pandavas' heroism and strength, especially the twins, Bhima and Arjuna, and predicts his army will be wiped out, regretting that he did not heed his friends' advice.
shots.B03C051S01H02: Sanjaya replies that Krishna came to the forest, promised to restore Yudhishthira's kingdom and to slay Duryodhana and his allies in a single day when the term ends, and that Draupadi's allies also vowed revenge. Yudhishthira asked Krishna to keep this promise when the thirteen years are over.
shots.B03C051S01H03: Dhritarashtra recalls Vidura's warning that the dice game would bring a terrible bloodshed that would destroy the Kurus, and says it is about to come true.

B03C052.summary: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did while Arjuna was away. Bhima urges Yudhishthira to leave the forest and attack the Kauravas before the term ends, arguing that deceit may be met with deceit and that the thirteen years may be counted loosely. Yudhishthira refuses to break his word, and when he laments his wretched state, the sage Vrihadaswa offers the tale of King Nala, who suffered even more.

scenes.B03C052S01: Janamejaya asks about the brothers while Arjuna is away, Bhima urges action against the Kauravas, and Yudhishthira refuses to break his word.
scenes.B03C052S02: Yudhishthira laments his fate to the sage Vrihadaswa, who offers the story of Nala as a more wretched case.

shots.B03C052S01H01: Section heading: the Nalopakhyana Parva, the Tale of Nala.
shots.B03C052S01H02: Janamejaya asks what Yudhishthira and his brothers did while Arjuna was in Indra's realm.
shots.B03C052S01H03: Vaisampayana says the brothers and Draupadi grieved for Arjuna. Bhima urges Yudhishthira to leave the forest, fight the Kauravas before the term ends, and count the thirteen years loosely.
shots.B03C052S01H04: Yudhishthira calms Bhima, promising he will defeat Duryodhana when the term ends, but saying he cannot lie or break his word.
shots.B03C052S01H05: The sage Vrihadaswa arrives. Yudhishthira honours him and speaks to him in sorrow.
shots.B03C052S02H01: Yudhishthira laments that he was cheated at dice, that his wife was dragged into the assembly, and that he is exiled in the forest in deerskins. He asks whether any king has ever been more wretched.
shots.B03C052S02H02: Vrihadaswa says he will tell of a king more wretched than Yudhishthira.
shots.B03C052S02H03: Yudhishthira asks for the story of that king.
shots.B03C052S02H04: Vrihadaswa names Nala, son of Virasena and king of the Nishadhas, who lost his kingdom at dice to Pushkara and lived in the forest with his wife, without servants, brothers or friends. He tells Yudhishthira that he has the support of his brothers and priests, and so should not grieve.
shots.B03C052S02H05: Yudhishthira asks Vrihadaswa to tell the story of Nala in full.

B03C053.summary: Vrihadaswa describes Nala as a virtuous and skilled king of the Nishadhas, and Bhima, king of Vidarbha, who through a sage's boon has a daughter, Damayanti, and three sons. Damayanti is unmatched in beauty, and Nala is peerless too. Hearing of each other from bards, they fall in love, and Nala catches a golden swan that promises to praise him to Damayanti.

scenes.B03C053S01: Vrihadaswa describes Nala and Damayanti, their mutual love from report alone, and the golden swan that carries Nala's praise to Damayanti.

shots.B03C053S01H01: Vrihadaswa describes Nala's virtues and Bhima's daughter Damayanti, whose beauty is unmatched, and how the two fall in love through the reports of heralds. Nala catches a golden swan that promises to speak well of him to Damayanti, and it flies to Vidarbha and praises him to her.

B03C054.summary: Damayanti pines for Nala, and her father Bhima announces a swayamvara, a ceremony at which a bride chooses her husband, inviting all kings. The sages Narada and Parvata tell Indra about the ceremony in heaven. The gods set out for Vidarbha, and on the road they meet Nala, dazzled by his beauty, and ask him to act as their messenger.

scenes.B03C054S01: Damayanti pines, her father calls a swayamvara, Narada reports it to Indra, and the gods set out and ask Nala to carry their message.

shots.B03C054S01H01: Damayanti, lovesick, grows pale, sighs and weeps. Her attendants tell her father, who decides his daughter is ready for marriage and summons all the kings to a swayamvara.
shots.B03C054S01H02: The sages Narada and Parvata visit Indra's court. Indra asks for news, and Narada tells him that Damayanti's swayamvara is near and that kings from every quarter are heading there.
shots.B03C054S01H03: Indra and the guardians of the world set out for Vidarbha. On the way they see Nala, struck by his beauty, and ask him to carry their message to Damayanti.

B03C055.summary: Nala agrees to carry the gods' message, reluctantly, and they reveal themselves as Indra, Agni, Varuna and Yama. The gods ask him to tell Damayanti to choose one of them as husband. Nala enters the guarded palace by their power and finds Damayanti, who is dazzled by him and asks who he is.

scenes.B03C055S01: The gods reveal themselves and ask Nala to carry their message, and Nala enters Damayanti's palace and introduces himself.

shots.B03C055S01H01: Nala asks who the gods are and what they want. Indra names himself, Agni, Varuna and Yama, and asks Nala to tell Damayanti to choose one of them as husband. Nala protests that he is in love himself, but the gods insist that he keep his promise.
shots.B03C055S01H02: Nala enters the guarded palace by the gods' power and sees Damayanti, whose beauty humbles the moon, surrounded by her attendants, who marvel at him. Damayanti asks who he is and why he has come, and Nala says he is a messenger of the gods, asking her to choose one of them.

B03C056.summary: Damayanti tells Nala that she chooses him, pleading with him to love her, and says she would rather die than be refused. Nala warns that refusing the gods is dangerous and urges her to choose one of them. Damayanti refuses, and Nala, bound by his promise, reports back to the gods that she will choose him at the swayamvara in their presence, without blame to him.

scenes.B03C056S01: Damayanti declares her choice of Nala, Nala urges her to pick a god, she refuses, and Nala reports back to the gods that the choice will be made at the swayamvara.

shots.B03C056S01H01: Damayanti bows to the gods and tells Nala she chooses him, pleading for his love and threatening to end her life if he refuses. Nala answers that the gods are worthy of her and urges her to choose one of them, but she insists, and he agrees to report back, and the gods ask him what happened, and he tells them she will choose him at the swayamvara in their presence, so that no blame falls on him.

B03C057.summary: At Bhima's swayamvara, Damayanti sees five men who look exactly like Nala and prays that the gods reveal her true husband. The gods reveal their true forms, and she chooses the real Nala by the signs of a mortal, placing a garland on him. The gods grant the couple boons, and Nala and Damayanti rule happily and have children.

scenes.B03C057S01: The kings assemble, Damayanti cannot tell Nala from the gods, prays for the gods to reveal him, chooses Nala, and is married to him with the gods' boons.

shots.B03C057S01H01: Vrihadaswa describes the kings gathering for Damayanti's swayamvara, her entrance, and her confusion at seeing five men who all look like Nala. She prays to the gods to show their true forms, and by the signs of mortality she chooses Nala, garlanding him, and the gods grant the couple boons. Nala and Damayanti then live happily, rule well, and have a son and a daughter.

B03C058.summary: On the way home from the swayamvara, the gods meet Kali and Dvapara, who had hoped to win Damayanti. Kali is furious that she chose a mortal and vows to ruin Nala. The gods rebuke Kali for wanting to curse so virtuous a king, but Kali enlists Dvapara to enter the dice and help him possess Nala.

scenes.B03C058S01: Indra meets Kali and Dvapara, who are furious that Damayanti chose Nala, and the gods rebuke them before Kali plans his revenge.

shots.B03C058S01H01: On the road home, Indra meets Kali and Dvapara, who are going to the swayamvara. Indra says it is already over, and Kali, angry, says that Damayanti should suffer for choosing a mortal. The gods rebuke Kali for wanting to curse so virtuous a king, and Kali then asks Dvapara to enter the dice so he can take Nala's kingdom.

B03C059.summary: Kali waits for an opening and finds it in the twelfth year, when Nala fails to wash his feet before his evening prayers. Possessed by Kali, Nala is challenged to dice by Pushkara, and he loses his stakes, despite the pleas of his citizens and his wife. The play goes on for months, and Nala is always the loser.

scenes.B03C059S01: Kali possesses Nala through a lapse, Pushkara challenges him to dice, and Nala loses over many months while his citizens fail to persuade him to stop.

shots.B03C059S01H01: Kali waits for a chance and enters Nala when he fails to wash his feet before prayers. Possessed, Nala is challenged by Pushkara and loses his wealth, his cars and his robes, and the citizens are unable to persuade him to stop, and his wife's pleas go unheard, so that the play goes on for months with Nala always losing.

B03C060.summary: Damayanti sees that Nala is ruined and tries to rouse him through his councillors, and when that fails, she summons the charioteer Varshneya. She sends their children to her kinsfolk in Vidarbha with the charioteer and his horses. Varshneya takes the children to Vidarbha and then leaves for Ayodhya, where he enters the service of King Rituparna.

scenes.B03C060S01: Damayanti sends for the councillors and the charioteer, and the charioteer takes the children away and enters the service of King Rituparna.

shots.B03C060S01H01: Damayanti, seeing Nala lose everything, asks her nurse to summon the councillors, but Nala ignores her. She then asks the charioteer Varshneya to take the children to her kinsfolk, leaving the horses and car, and he goes to Vidarbha and then to Ayodhya, where he serves King Rituparna.

B03C061.summary: Pushkara takes Nala's remaining wealth and then taunts him by proposing Damayanti as the next stake. Nala strips off his ornaments and leaves the city with Damayanti, wearing one cloth, but the citizens are forbidden to help them. Starving in the forest, Nala tries to catch golden birds, which are the dice in disguise and steal his cloth, and Damayanti offers to take him to her father's kingdom.

scenes.B03C061S01: Pushkara wins everything and proposes Damayanti as a stake, Nala leaves the city with her in one cloth, starves, and the golden birds steal his cloth, after which Damayanti suggests the road to Vidarbha.

shots.B03C061S01H01: Pushkara wins Nala's remaining kingdom and mocks him by proposing Damayanti as the next stake. Nala, enraged but silent, strips off his ornaments and leaves the city with Damayanti in a single cloth, while Pushkara forbids anyone to help him. Starving, Nala tries to catch golden birds with his cloth, but they are the dice in disguise and fly off with it, and Nala points out the roads, and Damayanti urges him to go with her to Vidarbha.

B03C062.summary: Nala refuses to go to Vidarbha, saying he will not appear in disgrace before the family that once saw him in glory. While Damayanti sleeps in a shelter, Nala, pressed by Kali, decides to desert her. He cuts her garment in half to cover himself, returns in grief, and then leaves her sleeping alone in the forest.

scenes.B03C062S01: Nala refuses Damayanti's plan to go to Vidarbha, and as she sleeps in a shelter, he cuts her garment and abandons her in the forest.

shots.B03C062S01H01: Nala says that he will not go to her father's kingdom in disgrace, since he once went there in glory and does not want to cause her sorrow.
shots.B03C062S01H02: Nala comforts his wife and they reach a travellers' shelter, where they sleep on the bare earth. Nala, under Kali's influence, takes a sword and cuts her cloth in half, then leaves her sleeping, returns in grief, and finally walks away from her in the forest.

B03C063.summary: Damayanti wakes alone in the forest and cries out for Nala, who has deserted her. Wandering in grief, she is seized by a huge serpent, and she weeps for Nala even as she is held. A hunter kills the serpent and frees her, but when he tries to force himself on her she curses him, and he falls dead.

scenes.B03C063S01: Damayanti wakes to find Nala gone, is seized by a serpent, is freed by a hunter, and curses the hunter when he tries to assault her.

shots.B03C063S01H01: Damayanti wakes alone, cries out for Nala, and wanders in grief and fear, while a serpent seizes her and she laments for her husband. A hunter kills the serpent and frees her, but when he tries to force himself on her she curses him, and he falls dead.

B03C064.summary: Damayanti wanders the wild forest alone in search of Nala, lamenting to beasts, mountains and trees, and describing her royal family. Holy ascetics welcome her, and after predicting that she will find her husband they vanish. She reaches a merchants' caravan led by Suchi, who has not seen Nala, and learns that it is bound for the city of Suvahu in the land of the Chedis.

scenes.B03C064S01: Damayanti searches the forest and laments, meets ascetics who foretell her reunion and then vanish, and finds a caravan whose leader has not seen Nala.

shots.B03C064S01H01: Damayanti wanders through the wild forest, passing trees, beasts and rivers, and sits down to lament. She calls on Nala, pleads with a mountain and a tiger for news, and describes her father, her husband and their royal families.
shots.B03C064S01H02: She goes north to a hermitage of ascetics, who welcome her and ask who she is. She tells them her story and her search for Nala.
shots.B03C064S01H03: The ascetics foretell that she will see Nala again, and then they vanish with their sacred fires and asylum.
shots.B03C064S01H04: Puzzled and grieving, Damayanti addresses an Ashoka tree and then goes on to a merchants' caravan. Its leader, Suchi, says he has not seen Nala, and that the caravan is bound for Suvahu, the city of the Chedi king.

B03C065.summary: The merchant caravan camps by a lotus lake, where a herd of wild elephants stampedes through the sleeping men and kills many. The survivors blame the strange woman who joined them, and Damayanti laments her misfortunes as the fruit of sins. She reaches the Chedi capital of Suvahu, where the queen mother takes her in as a companion to her daughter on her own conditions.

scenes.B03C065S01: The caravan is trampled by elephants and blames Damayanti, Damayanti laments, and she is taken in at the Chedi palace on her own conditions.

shots.B03C065S01H01: The caravan camps at a fragrant lotus lake. At midnight a herd of wild elephants stampedes through the sleeping merchants and kills many. The survivors blame the strange woman who joined them, and Damayanti, terrified and ashamed, flees into the woods and laments her ill fortune as the fruit of sins.
shots.B03C065S01H02: Next morning the survivors leave, mourning their dead. Damayanti laments again, reaches the Chedi city of Suvahu in a single garment, and is noticed by the queen mother, who sends for her. Damayanti tells her story of the dice game and of Nala's desertion of her.
shots.B03C065S01H03: The queen mother offers to have her men search for Nala, and asks Damayanti to stay. Damayanti sets conditions: she will not serve, be pursued by men, or eat leftovers, and she wants to meet the Brahmanas searching for her husband.
shots.B03C065S01H04: The queen mother agrees and gives Damayanti to her daughter Sunanda as a companion, and Damayanti lives there with her needs met.

B03C066.summary: Nala sees a fire in the forest and hears a snake, Karkotaka, calling for help. Cursed by the sage Narada, the snake asks Nala to carry him out of the flames, and when Nala sets him down, the snake bites him and changes his appearance so he cannot be recognised. Karkotaka says the poison will torment the one who deceived Nala, gives him two garments that will restore his form, and tells him to go to King Rituparna at Ayodhya.

scenes.B03C066S01: Nala rescues the snake Karkotaka from a forest fire, is bitten and disguised, and is given garments and directions to Rituparna.

shots.B03C066S01H01: Nala rescues the snake Karkotaka from a fire, and the snake explains that he was cursed by Narada. Karkotaka bites Nala, disguising him, promises that the poison will torment the one who deceived him, gives him garments that will restore his form, and tells him to serve King Rituparna at Ayodhya.

B03C068.summary: King Bhima sends Brahmanas across the land to find Nala and Damayanti, offering great rewards. The Brahmana Sudeva finds Damayanti in the Chedi palace and recognises her by her beauty, even though she is worn and soiled. He tells her that her parents, brothers and children are alive and searching for her, and the queen mother asks him to tell her Damayanti's story.

scenes.B03C068S01: Bhima's searchers find Damayanti at the Chedi palace, Sudeva recognises her and gives her news of her family, and the queen mother asks for her story.

shots.B03C068S01H01: Bhima sends Brahmanas out in all directions with rich rewards to find Nala and Damayanti. The Brahmana Sudeva finds her in the Chedi palace beside Sunanda, recognises her though she is soiled and frail, and reflects on the beauty of her and the loss of her husband.
shots.B03C068S01H02: Sudeva greets Damayanti as the friend of her brother, and tells her that her parents, brothers and children are well, and that many Brahmanas are searching for her.
shots.B03C068S01H03: Damayanti weeps and asks after her family. Sunanda tells the queen mother, who asks Sudeva who Damayanti is and how she fell into this state, and Sudeva begins to tell the true story.

B03C067.summary: Nala reaches Ayodhya in disguise as Vahuka, a charioteer and cook, and is taken into the service of King Rituparna as superintendent of the stables. Each evening he recites a verse about his lost wife, and when Jivala asks him about it, he tells the story as if it were another man's. He lives there unknown, remembering Damayanti.

scenes.B03C067S01: Nala presents himself to Rituparna as Vahuka and is taken into service, then recites his nightly lament until Jivala asks about it.

shots.B03C067S01H01: On the tenth day Nala reaches Rituparna's city and offers his services as Vahuka, a charioteer, horse-trainer and cook. Rituparna accepts and makes him superintendent of the stables, with Varshneya and Jivala as companions.
shots.B03C067S01H02: Nala, living in the king's city, recites a verse each night lamenting his helpless wife. When Jivala asks whom he mourns, Nala answers with a story about a man who had a wife, was false to her, and lost her in the forest.
shots.B03C067S01H03: Nala lives on in the king's service, unknown, remembering Damayanti.
